verdict.rationale: iTerm2's own docs say a tab can be divided into any number of vertical and horizontal panes, each running its own session. Its README describes a native window/tab/pane hierarchy, and Global Search and Open Quickly let you find and navigate across tabs, all without tmux. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of pane and tab workflows, detailed documentation of tab organization (reordering, naming, pane navigation shortcuts).

support.subject: As a developer, I can split windows into panes and organize work across tabs without an external multiplexer

citations.quote: Divide a tab up into multiple panes, each one showing a different session. You can slice vertically and horizontally and create any number of panes in any imaginable arrangement.
Browser profiles integrate web browsing into iTerm2's window/tab/pane hierarchy.
Cmd-Shift-O opens a search across all sessions by tab title, command, hostname, directory, or badge. Navigate large session collections instantly.
Search all your tabs at once with Global Search.
